title: Paper 1 style section: Sunrise Bakery (25 minutes)
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 47 (Pupil PDF worksheet: own exam-style questions, case data and mark-scheme points (teacher-written))
intro: Lesson 47. Answer every question; self-mark with the mark scheme and add errors to your repair list. All businesses, people and figures in these cases are fictional, made up for practice.

passage.title: Sunrise Bakery
paras: Sunrise Bakery is a sole trader business owned by Maryam in Leicester. She employs 4 staff and sells bread and cakes from one shop. Each week she sells 1,200 loaves at £2.50 each. Her weekly total costs are £2,100. Rent is £400 a week. A supermarket with an in-store bakery is opening nearby next month. Maryam is choosing between hiring a delivery driver (£420 a week) and using a delivery app that takes 25% of each order.

questions.q: State one fixed cost for Sunrise Bakery.
questions.a: Rent (£400 a week) or staff salaries.

questions.q: Calculate the weekly revenue from loaves.
Explain one benefit to Maryam of being a sole trader.
questions.a: She keeps all the profit (1), so the £900 a week is hers (1), giving her a reward for her work (1). Or: makes decisions quickly.

questions.q: Explain one way Maryam could improve her cash flow.
questions.a: Ask suppliers for longer to pay (1), so cash stays in the business longer (1), helping her pay rent on time (1).

questions.q: Analyse the impact on Sunrise Bakery of the supermarket opening nearby.
questions.a: Level-marked (6): lower prices may draw customers away, revenue falls below £3,000; but Maryam can stress fresh, local, specialist halal products and service.

questions.q: Justify whether Maryam should hire a delivery driver or use a delivery app.
questions.a: Level-marked (9): driver is a fixed £420 a week, better if delivery sales exceed £1,680 a week (25% of 1,680 = 420); app has no fixed cost and suits low or uncertain demand.

markScheme.a: Level 3 (5-6): two developed chains of reasoning, both in context. Level 2 (3-4): developed reasoning, partly in context. Level 1 (1-2): points identified with little development. Level 3 (7-9): a justified choice using the data, developed chains of reasoning, and a comparison showing why it beats the other option. Level 2 (4-6): reasons in context, little comparison. Level 1 (1-3): generic points.
